question.text: A portfolio of 4 bonds has weights 25% each. The individual YTMs are 7%, 7.5%, 8%, and 8.5%. The portfolio's weighted-average YTM is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: With equal 25% weights, the portfolio yield is the simple weighted average of the four YTMs: 0.25 x 7.0 + 0.25 x 7.5 + 0.25 x 8.0 + 0.25 x 8.5 = 1.75 + 1.875 + 2.0 + 2.125 = 7.75%. The Trap: 7.50% is just the mid-range of the two extremes; 8.00% picks the centre of the upper half; 7.25% effectively drops two bonds. None of these reflect a weighted-average across all four equally-weighted holdings. Note: Pages 336-337 of the workbook illustrate the same weighted-average yield calculation for a fixed-income portfolio.
